Consider me somewhere halfway between a proper prepper and the unprepared masses. I don't really have the budget to commit to the lifestyle, but the old boyscout motto of "Be Prepared" has always stuck with me, so I've got a little bit of preparedness for almost any contingency.

I think camping and hiking are a great way to be ready for a collapse without going all-in on the lifestyle. It promotes useful survival skills and abilities, it encourages fitness, gives you a taste of what the world is like away from civilization, and many of the items required are very dual-purpose. If someone's skeptical of the need to be prepared for a crisis, they might not be as resistant to the idea of going camping or hiking. And, if I'm lucky enough to live a life where this sort of preparedness is never really required, well, my investment in camping gear is worth it just for those outings.

Not likely. The scare of what would happen if there wasn't net neutrality is pretty well overblown; we didn't have it until pretty recently & there was no blocking of websites happening. There may have been some cases of selective slowdowns but even then they were pretty rare.
